label: A Line Through the Origin
subgoals: Two quantities are proportional when their graph is a straight line through the origin.
A point such as (4, 10) means that four units of the first quantity correspond to ten of the second, so the constant is 10/4 = 2.
A line that does not pass through the origin describes a relationship with an initial amount, not a proportional one.

label: Reading Points
subgoals: Each point on the graph is a pair of corresponding values.
The unit rate is the y-coordinate when x equals one.
Tables, equations and graphs describe the same relationship.

label: Comparing Relationships
subgoals: Two proportional graphs can be compared by their slopes.
If one graph passes through (1, 3) and another through (1, 5), the second represents a faster rate.
A graph that starts at a positive y-intercept is not proportional, even when it is a straight line.
